options.text: Use 3, because the immediate reward is undiscounted and the terminal state has no continuation value to add.
options.rationale: The Bellman target is reward plus gamma times continuation value, and the terminal continuation is zero.

options.text: Use 2.7, because gamma first multiplies the reward produced directly by the current action before any continuation is considered.
options.rationale: The current reward has delay zero and coefficient one; gamma multiplies the next-state continuation term.

options.text: Use the reward from the action before this one, because a terminal reward belongs to the latest prior action rather than the current backup.
options.rationale: The stated transition reward is attached to the current state-action transition and enters its backup directly.

options.text: Use 3 divided by 0.1, because gamma represents termination probability and a terminal observation expands into an infinite expected reward stream.
options.rationale: The observed transition already ends the episode, so there is no future stream to geometrically sum.

questions.stem: A news system replaces a broad exploration policy with one that shows mostly sports articles. A month later, its log contains mostly reactions to sports. Which conclusion respects how the policy generated this evidence?

options.text: The new reaction distribution is externally fixed, because content choices change immediate clicks without changing which feedback observations enter later logs.
options.rationale: Showing sports creates opportunities to observe sports reactions while withholding comparable feedback about other content.

options.text: The policy changed its own observation distribution; comparisons need logged propensities, overlap, experimentation, or defensible assumptions about unshown content.
options.rationale: Action selection controls which outcomes can be observed, so policy evaluation must address this endogenous missing data.

options.text: A reward predictor accurate on displayed sports articles identifies reactions to unshown topics, so policy support is unnecessary for evaluating broader recommendations.
options.rationale: In-support prediction quality does not validate counterfactual outcomes where the new log supplies little or no exposure.

options.text: Replace the policy with uniform random recommendations indefinitely, because equal exposure is the intrinsically optimal reward-information tradeoff for this system.
options.rationale: Random exposure can restore support, but uncertainty-aware or constrained exploration may obtain useful evidence at lower reward cost.

questions.stem: Two random variables have the same mean and variance but different distribution shapes. Without further information, which statement about their expected values after applying a nonlinear function h is justified?

options.text: Their transformed expectations equal h of the shared mean, because expectation passes through a nonlinear function when first moments match.
options.rationale: Expectation commutes generally with affine functions, not with an arbitrary nonlinear transformation.

options.text: Their transformed expectations match because equal variance captures the distributional information needed for the expectation of any nonlinear function.
options.rationale: Nonlinear expectations can depend on higher moments, tails, asymmetry, or other features not fixed by mean and variance.

options.text: Their transformed expectations can differ, because h averages over the full outcome distributions and matching two moments does not determine that average.
options.rationale: Different shapes with common first and second moments can assign different mass where a nonlinear function is large.

options.text: Their transformed expectations are the transformed most-likely outcomes, because an expected value represents the mode before and after applying h.
options.rationale: A mean need not be a mode or even a possible outcome, and transformation does not create that identity.

questions.stem: A naive Bayes model treats two word indicators as independent after conditioning on whether an email is spam. Each word is more common in spam. Before the class is known, how are the indicators generally related?

options.text: They remain marginally independent, because conditional independence persists when the unknown spam class is averaged out of the joint distribution.
options.rationale: Mixing class-conditional distributions with different word rates generally induces marginal association between the indicators.

options.text: They remain unrelated through the class, because a shared latent spam status changes each word rate without inducing association between observed words.
options.rationale: Variation in a shared latent class moves both word probabilities and can therefore associate their observed occurrences.

options.text: They have identical class-conditional frequencies, because conditional independence requires both word indicators to use the same conditional distribution.
options.rationale: Conditional independence factorizes the joint distribution but permits distinct word probabilities within each class.

options.text: They are generally positively associated: observing one word raises spam belief, which raises the predictive probability of observing the other word.
options.rationale: Marginal association can arise through the unobserved class even though the naive Bayes factorization holds within each class.

options.text: Send observations left when Fahrenheit temperature is at most 68, since the increasing conversion preserves order and translates the threshold.

options.rationale: Order-based tree splits can be translated across increasing unit conversions without standardizing the feature.

options.text: No equivalent stump exists, because converting Celsius to Fahrenheit changes the information content available to a threshold-based learner.
options.rationale: The conversion is invertible and preserves information as well as order; only its numerical coordinate representation changes.

options.text: Keep gamma fixed, because rescaling coordinates changes their notation without changing the pairwise distance geometry used by the kernel.
options.rationale: Centimeter differences are one hundred times meter differences, so their squared distances are ten thousand times larger.

questions.stem: A cluster consists of many nearby customer profiles plus one extreme profile. Why can replacing a squared-distance centroid update with a medoid update reduce the extreme profile's influence?

options.text: Both centers have equal outlier sensitivity, because an arithmetic centroid is already robust to a single distant assigned observation.
options.rationale: A distant point can move the arithmetic mean substantially because squared deviations give it high leverage.

options.text: A medoid estimates the highest density mode, so its robustness follows from converting the clustering objective into a density estimator.
options.rationale: A medoid minimizes aggregate dissimilarity over candidate observations; it does not inherently estimate a density mode.

options.text: A medoid is an observed profile minimizing unsquared dissimilarities, so one extreme distance has less leverage than under a squared-distance mean.
options.rationale: The changed representative and loss geometry reduce the quadratic amplification responsible for centroid sensitivity.

options.text: Zero-one and log loss have the same finite optimizer because they assign equal empirical risk to coefficient vectors producing equal hard labels.

options.text: The conditional probabilities also determine feature density, so the classifier directly supports both class decisions and likelihood-based novelty detection.
